category_title: Pre-engaged students with organizational and focus challenges
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-class literacy lesson at the beginning of the school year with the goal of seeing themselves as a reader.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, it is time for our whole-class literacy lesson. Please sit and listen to the instruction so we can practice seeing ourselves as readers.

STUDENT: I came to school to learn!

TUTOR: That is great. Now please focus on what I am saying.

STUDENT: (Wiggles around and points at a neighbor) Look at what he is doing.

TUTOR: Please keep your eyes up here and listen to the lesson.

STUDENT: (Picks up a found piece of string from the floor and starts twisting it around his fingers, completely fascinated by it instead of the teacher)

options.A: Provide individual storage space for the student, such as chair bags or desks with compartments, to help keep their materials organized during the whole-class literacy lessons.
options.B: Integrate multicultural picture books, particularly African American stories, into the whole-class literacy lessons to use as reading materials during instruction throughout the school year.
options.C: Continuously remind the class that they are expected to be ready to at least show they are participating during the literacy lesson, even if they do not know the answer or are not completely comfortable with what is being learned.
options.D: Incorporate the student's specific interests, such as their fascination with found objects like pieces of string, into the instructional materials used during the whole-class literacy lessons.
